params.body:
Six tasks say "set DNS records" and eight say "write a content security policy". Elixir derives the first line now (elixir#210, #211) and measures what a policy would have to allow (elixir#209) — and all of it sat in a JSON report nobody opens.

- **Mail authentication** carries the record to paste (`v=spf1 include:… ~all`, `v=DMARC1; p=none`) and, where there is one, the doubt underneath it: where the mail arrives, that we do not know that name as a sender, and what to do if it does send.
- **Exposure**, while the policy is missing, carries what the page loads today: per third-party host the kinds it is referenced as, plus how much inline script and style the page carries, because a policy without `'unsafe-inline'` breaks exactly those. A site that already sends a policy gets none of this: there is nothing left to weigh.

None of these lines carries severity. A draft is not a verdict, and whoever publishes it decides.

Tests: the record and its doubt on the mail card, the sources and the inline count on the exposure card, and silence where a policy already exists. Suite green but `BuildStampTest` (worktree only).
params.title: Het werk staat op de kaart, niet in een rapport
